Created a game-ready rugged military supply crate in Blender 5.3 and exported it for Godot 4.

### Deliverables
- **Main glTF 2.0 Binary**: [military_supply_crate.glb](file:///home/agent/project/output/military_supply_crate.glb) (1.6 MB; embedded textures)
  - `MilitarySupplyCrate` (`1,392` triangles): kit-bashed from recessed body/lid panels with reinforcement ribs, rubber lid gasket, bottom skid runners, 8 riveted corner guards, 2 front draw latches, 2 rear strap hinges, and 2 side U-bar handles.
  - `MilitarySupplyCrate-col` (`12` triangles): bounding-box collision mesh named with Godot's `-col` suffix.
- **Optional LODs**:
  - [military_supply_crate_LOD1.glb](file:///home/agent/project/output/military_supply_crate_LOD1.glb) (`696` triangles)
  - [military_supply_crate_LOD2.glb](file:///home/agent/project/output/military_supply_crate_LOD2.glb) (`400` triangles)
- **PBR Texture Maps (`1024×1024` PNG)** in [output/textures/](file:///home/agent/project/output/textures):
  - [military_crate_basecolor.png](file:///home/agent/project/output/textures/military_crate_basecolor.png) (olive-drab paint, weathered tactical stencils, bare-metal edge chips, crevice/ground dust, gunmetal guards, steel hardware)
  - [military_crate_normal.png](file:///home/agent/project/output/textures/military_crate_normal.png) (tangent-space surface grain and chip micro-relief)
  - [military_crate_orm.png](file:///home/agent/project/output/textures/military_crate_orm.png) (R = Ambient Occlusion, G = Roughness, B = Metallic)

### Verification Results
Checked directly against the exported `.glb` binaries and `.png` headers:
- **Scale & Alignment (`+Y` up)**: `0.8388 m × 0.4200 m × 0.5296 m`, `min_Y = 0.00000`, centered at `X = 0.00000, Z = 0.00000` (same centering/grounding verified on LOD1 and LOD2).
- **Triangle Budget**: `1,392` main triangles (`1,404` total with `-col`), well within the `3,000` triangle limit.
- **UVs & Tangents**: All meshes in main, `-col`, LOD1, and LOD2 contain `TEXCOORD_0` inside `[0, 1]` with `0` overlapping triangles and exported `TANGENT` attributes.
- **Materials**: `1` PBR metallic-roughness material (`M_MilitaryCrate`) wired to `baseColorTexture`, `normalTexture`, `metallicRoughnessTexture`, and `occlusionTexture`.

### Notes / Limitations
- Only `BLENDER_EEVEE` was available in this headless Blender build (Cycles baking was unavailable), so the `1024×1024` PBR textures were synthesized procedurally in 3D crate space via UV rasterization in Python/NumPy and inspected in Blender `rendered` viewport captures.

I have created and exported the game-ready cast-iron fire hydrant prop for Godot 4.

### Delivered Files
- **Main asset**: [fire_hydrant.glb](file:///home/agent/project/output/fire_hydrant.glb) (`3,820` triangles)
- **Optional LODs**:
  - [fire_hydrant_LOD1.glb](file:///home/agent/project/output/fire_hydrant_LOD1.glb) (`1,719` triangles)
  - [fire_hydrant_LOD2.glb](file:///home/agent/project/output/fire_hydrant_LOD2.glb) (`824` triangles)
- **PBR Textures (`1024×1024` PNG)**:
  - [fire_hydrant_basecolor.png](file:///home/agent/project/output/textures/fire_hydrant_basecolor.png) (sRGB base color)
  - [fire_hydrant_normal.png](file:///home/agent/project/output/textures/fire_hydrant_normal.png) (tangent-space normal map with baked sand-cast iron texture and edge bevels)
  - [fire_hydrant_orm.png](file:///home/agent/project/output/textures/fire_hydrant_orm.png) (packed ORM: `R`=Ambient Occlusion, `G`=Roughness, `B`=Metallic)

### Asset & Verification Summary
- **Geometry & Scale**: Real-world scale in metres (`0.856 m` tall, `[-0.2002, 0, -0.1833]` to `[0.2002, 0.856, 0.1833]` in glTF `+Y`-up coordinates), lowest point at `Y = 0`, horizontally centered at `(0.0, 0.0)`. Includes base, waist, and bonnet flanges with 18 hex bolts, top pentagon operating nut, front pumper and left hose nozzles with bolted pentagon-nut caps, an open brass-threaded right hose nozzle, and an interlocking 10-link steel chain suspending the hanging bolted nozzle cap.
- **UVs & Material**: Single non-overlapping `TEXCOORD_0` UV layout inside `[0.0074, 0.9926]` (zero degenerate UV triangles) and a single `CastIronHydrant` PBR metallic-roughness material with `POSITION`, `NORMAL`, `TEXCOORD_0`, and `TANGENT` attributes.
- **Optional items omitted**: A `-col` collision mesh was not added inside [fire_hydrant.glb](file:///home/agent/project/output/fire_hydrant.glb) (collision shape can be generated on import in Godot 4).

rows.rule: The cell's first session ended 'finished' with a main GLB, without a continuation session.

rows.label: Time to a delivered package (s)
rows.rule: Wall seconds of every session of the cell, summed.

rows.label: Model calls / tokens / images
rows.rule: The relay's ledger for the cell's accounts: model calls, tokens (input + output + thinking), generated images.

rows.label: Loads in Godot 4
rows.rule: Stock Godot 4.7 imports the bare GLB (GLB and its referenced files only) without error (GodotValidator).

rows.label: Loads in three.js
rows.rule: The three.js check on the bare GLB reports no failed check.

rows.label: Independent Blender check passes
rows.rule: The upstream qa_check script reports pass.

rows.label: Scale and orientation right
rows.rule: Largest dimension inside the brief's plausible range, and for an upright brief, tallest along +Y.

rows.label: Grounded and centred
rows.rule: Lowest point within 2 cm of y = 0; bounding-box centre within 10 % of the largest dimension of the origin in x and z.

rows.label: Triangle budget met
rows.rule: Visible triangles of the main GLB at most the brief's budget.

rows.label: UVs present, inside 0-1, not overlapping
rows.rule: Every primitive has TEXCOORD_0; no UV vertex outside [0, 1] (1e-4 slack); per material, at most 1 % of the covered texels are covered twice (a 256 px raster of the triangles).

rows.label: Texel density even
rows.rule: For every visible object, the upstream texel_density script's spread (largest island density / smallest) is at most 2.

rows.label: Base colour, normal and metal-roughness maps present and not blank
rows.rule: Every material binds the three maps (pbr_complete); no base-colour or normal map is flat (all channels' standard deviation under 1 %); no base colour is black (95 % of texels under 30 of 255).

rows.label: LOD files present and valid
rows.rule: At least one <name>_LOD<n>.glb beside the main GLB; each readable and with fewer triangles than the level before.

rows.label: Collision present and simple
rows.rule: A collision mesh (a node named as one in the main GLB, or a collision file beside it); every one convex (its volume within 2 % of its hull's) with at most 255 vertices (PhysX's hull limit; Godot simplifies larger ones itself).

rows.label: Game-ready rate
rows.rule: Share of the game-ready checks above that pass; 'all' when every one does.

rows.label: Draw calls / materials
rows.rule: Primitives drawn (one draw call each) and materials, main GLB.

rows.label: Triangles per level
rows.rule: Visible triangles of the main GLB, then of each LOD file.

rows.label: Texture memory
rows.rule: From each image's size and channels with a full mip chain: uncompressed RGBA8, and Godot 4's default VRAM compression on desktop (0.5 byte per texel, 1 with alpha or for a normal map). An estimate from the files.

rows.label: Package bytes
rows.rule: Every file under the main GLB's folder (hidden caches excluded).

rows.label: Blind pairwise judge
rows.rule: Per other arm: the winner both orders agree on, 'tie', or 'split'.

rows.label: Reads at game size
rows.rule: The same judge on 128 px views (and the lowest LOD's, where delivered), both orders.

rows.label: One change request to a new delivered package
rows.rule: A new session over a copy of the cell's files asked the brief's change (CHANGES): delivered or not, wall seconds, model calls, tokens.

rows.label: The change left everything else alone
rows.rule: package_diff of the two GLBs: parts resized by the asked ratio (within 0.1) against everything else that changed, was added or removed; triangles and bounds before and after. Pass: at least one part on target and no collateral.

rows.label: Hand steps left before it is in a level (Godot 4)

LOD files are not a step: Godot generates levels on import, and delivered ones are used only when wired (shown, not counted). An install whose in-engine checks all pass covers collision and levels.
